h: Teshuvah Awakens Joy and Renewed Strength in Divine Service

p: "She considers a field and takes it (Mishlei 31:16-17);
from the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard.
She girds her loins with strength
In Toras Kohanim on this parsha:
A parable: a king who was angry with his wife
after some days he was reconciled with her;
when they saw that the Omnipresent was reconciled
And this is what is said, "She considers a field and takes it":
this is a field of apples
"From the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה ה, ז)
in the manner of what is said (Yeshayahu 5:7):
כִּי כֶרֶם ה׳ צְבָאוֹת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳
"For the vineyard of Hashem of Hosts is the House of Yisrael," etc.
to serve before the Holy One, blessed be He,
along the lines of what is said
"The place of the masters of teshuvah," etc.,
"because they are closer to the King
with greater desire of the heart
to draw near to the King."
And this is what is said, "a woman of valor,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג מב, ב)
as is said in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 42b);
אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳ וְגוֹ׳ (מִשְׁלֵי לא, ל)
and through fear one comes to teshuvah
where fear is expounded as teshuvah).
"She considers a field and takes it"
the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah.
"From the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard,"
And it says "from the fruit of her hands,"
"It is revealed and known before You
that I toiled with my ten fingers in Torah,"
though toil in Torah is with the mind
and the labor of the mouth;
by the name of the hands.
And it says "from the fruit of her hands,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שָׁם ה, א)
along the lines of what they said in the Gemara (Kesubos 5a):
"Greater are the deeds of the tzaddikim," etc.;
וְאִלּוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה יְדֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים כוּ׳
"whereas of the work of the hands of the tzaddikim," etc.:
מִקְּדָשׁ ה׳ כּוֹנְנוּ יָדֶיךָ (שְׁמוֹת טו, יז)
"'The Sanctuary, O Hashem, which Your hands established'" (Shemos 15:17).
the main service of man is
"in your mouth and in your heart" (Devarim 30:14),
to bring the words of Torah into the heart;
and afterward the completion of the deed
And for this reason it is written "to do it,"
"the work of the hands of the tzaddikim,"
and it is written, "which Your hands established";
that is, through words of Torah,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קכג, א
"From the fruit of her hands she plants a vineyard":
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה ה׳ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
that Hashem should dwell among the Children of Yisrael,
and the heart of Yisrael should be
to serve before the Holy One, blessed be He,
אַחַר שֶׁרָאוּ שֶׁנִּתְרַצָּה לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
after they saw that Hashem Yisbarach was reconciled with them,
in that He commanded to take the offerings
וַיִּקְחוּ אֵת אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה מֹשֶׁה וְגוֹ׳ (וַיִּקְרָא ט, ה)
"and they took that which Moshe commanded," etc. (Vayikra 9:5)
in joy, and stood before Him.
it does not say 'rejoiced' but 'let it rejoice':
they are destined to rejoice," etc.
"Those who keep Shabbos shall rejoice in Your Kingship":
the yoke of His Kingship, may He be blessed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית ח, ב וּפֵירוּשׁ רַשִׁ״י)
as they said (Taanis 8b, with Rashi's commentary):
"Those who fear My Name — those who keep Shabbos"
along the lines of what they said
"And I rejoiced out of my fear."
"The fear of Shabbos is upon the am ha'aretz."
And on Shabbos one merits teshuvah,
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem"
שֶׁכָּל מִי שֶׁמּוֹדֶה פְּשָׁעָיו וְעוֹזֵב כוּ׳
"whoever confesses his sins and forsakes them," etc.;
"He who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy."
